rubric.evidence: Every load-bearing claim traced to a primary source fetched live 2026-10-25: css-navigation-1 § 2.2 (matching rule and both spec examples quoted verbatim from the fetched ED), the current-navigation-state algorithm (fully-active check, pre-reveal activation state with null source element, loading→ready→committed phases, null when no ongoing navigate event), the route-matching explainer's link-matching section (cross-document window quote), the HTML Standard NavigateEvent IDL (readonly attribute Element? sourceElement — read from the fetched page), runtime_enabled_features.json5 (NavigationSourcePseudoClass stable, implied_by RouteMatching), BCD css/selectors/navigation-source.json, webstatus.dev 0-result query, the resolved blink-dev Intent-to-Ship thread, tracking bug, and both standards-position requests.

Feature id 6327898878377984 confirmed in the milestone=156 listing under 'Enabled by default' (fetched 2026-10-25); slug css-pseudo-class-for-navigation-source-element derived from the exact listing name 'CSS pseudo-class for navigation source element' per invariant #1; H1 uses the listing name. BCD independently records Chrome 156 for the selector, agreeing with the listing position.

The developer-facing surface is one argument-less pseudo-class plus the navigation-state matching model it depends on; both are inventoried in reference-contract.json with all nine dimensions mapped to rendered fragments on the overview (a single selector does not warrant child routes). The pre-reveal null-source-element subtlety (the destination page never matches) and the invalid-selector behavior in non-supporting browsers are documented rather than smoothed over.

The lifecycle table makes the six navigation moments and their matching outcomes explicit, including the two traps: rules comma-joined with :navigation-source are dropped entirely in non-supporting browsers (Selectors 4 invalid-selector handling, with the :is() forgiving-parsing mitigation named), and the destination page never sees a match (pre-reveal state carries a null source element).

Both spec examples quoted verbatim (view-transition-name thumbnail, form/submit outline) plus one gendn-derived loading-indicator example labelled as derived. Live showcase demo embedded (thumbnail-view-transition, HEAD 200 2026-10-25) with the three sibling concepts linked. Examples are source-derived but not executed in a Chrome 156 build in this environment (the verification container runs headless Chromium 140-line Playwright build, which predates the selector).

Real per-version BCD table (Chrome 156, Edge mirror, Firefox false, Safari false, experimental:true) with the BCD file linked; webstatus.dev 0-result query stated plainly with the query URL (no invented Baseline claim — banner says Limited availability, single-engine); both vendor positions linked; progressive-enhancement fallback behavior documented via the invalid-selector rule.

Zero plain-text citations; every source label links to the canonical original (csswg drafts anchors verified present in the fetched ED, html.spec.whatwg.org anchors verified against the fetched page source — dom-navigateevent-sourceelement, the-navigateevent-interface, navigation-activation-interface — Google Groups conversation URL resolved from the chromestatus msgid redirect, BCD blob, webstatus API, wpt.fyi directory, showcase feature + concept routes HEAD-checked 200).

Single h1, sequential h2/h3 outline, th scope via .doc-table header rows, baseline banner role=note with aria-label, iframe title + figcaption, all tables wrapped in .table-wrap for scroll without content loss.

CPS feature route HEAD-200 with four concept routes; thumbnail-view-transition (the spec's own motivating example) embedded as the selected demo via lazy iframe with the mandated sandbox + referrerpolicy pair; loading-links, form-submit-feedback and selector-parse-lab linked from the figcaption; caption notes Chrome 156+ requirement.

openQuestions: css-navigation-1 is an early Editor's Draft whose Privacy and Security sections read 'To be written.'; CSSWG review (and the open Mozilla/WebKit position requests) may change the matching model — the lifecycle table would need re-anchoring if the merged text differs.

Whether Chrome's shipped matching window for cross-document navigations exactly matches the explainer's 'ends in the first frame of the new page' wording was not re-verified against Chromium source in this run; the page attributes that claim to the explainer, not to Chrome.
The examples were not executed in a Chrome 156+ build in this environment (verification Chromium predates the selector); behavior is documented from the spec text.
